findings.body:
The new header is `vec![body.len() as u8]`. The `as u8` cast keeps only the low 8 bits of the length, so any body of 256 or more bytes gets a length byte that does not match its real size (for example, 256 bytes yields 0). The old 4-byte u32 header did not have this limit.

Trigger: Calling frame() with a body of 256 or more bytes, such as any normal-sized payload.

Impact: Any caller that frames a body longer than 255 bytes produces a corrupt frame with no error or panic. A decoder reading the length byte gets the wrong length and misparses the body and everything after it. Callers have no way to detect this from the return value.
findings.suggestion: Either return an error (or use Result) when body.len() > u8::MAX, or keep a wider length prefix such as the original u32 big-endian header.
findings.title: Length byte silently truncates bodies over 255 bytes

risk_level.reason: The frame header shrinks from a 4-byte u32 to a single byte via `body.len() as u8`, which silently truncates the length for bodies over 255 bytes and breaks the wire format for existing readers.
